response: Global management of colorectal cancer (CRC) with synchronous liver metastases (SLM) at the same centre is associated with fewer procedures. However, it does not significantly influence overall survival. The use of chemotherapy between procedures is increased, and there is a longer delay in treatment when surgery is performed at a different centre. This suggests that more rigorous selection of patients for surgery may contribute to higher disease-free survival rates after liver metastasis resection. Therefore, while global management at the same centre may have some benefits in terms of procedure reduction, its impact on overall survival is limited.
